newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia c.bank plans neutral Feb monetary policy.
newsitem.headline: Croatia c.bank plans neutral Feb monetary policy.

text.p: Croatia's central bank will pursue a "neutral" monetary policy in February, it said in a tightly worded statement on Thursday.
This would mean keeping the same relatively rigid stance it has had for the past three months, leaving key rates and reserve requirements unchanged after a series of small cuts in 1996.
The discount rate is now 6.5 percent and benchmark Lombard lending rate 11 percent.
But the bank said it may consider tightening monetary reins further to protect the price and exchange rate stability in case of a revived inflationary pressure.
Retail prices rose 1.0 percent last month, compared with 0.5 percent in December, and 4.2 percent year-on-year.
This was decribed by the bank as a one-off price increase, caused by mainly seasonal and climatic factors.
"Although price indicators were higher than in previous months...this requires no changes in the monetary policy, so it will be neutral in February," the central bank said.
It intervened in the money supply last month by draining kuna liquidity through a foreign exchange sale, but mentioned no such interventions this month.
The exchange rate of the domestic currency, the kuna, was described as "stable, with slight oscillations".
The National Bank of Croatia also praised a continued decline in commercial banks' lending rates as an encouraging factor for further economic development.
It said interest rates fell 1.7 percentage points recently. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
